findings.observed: The second put raises OverflowError only after appending. len(q) is 2, and after removing 'oldest', get() returns 'rejected'.
findings.expected: The second put raises OverflowError without changing the queue; len(q) remains 1 and only 'oldest' is queued.
findings.explanation: TaskQueue.put mutates _items before checking capacity, violating the required failure atomicity and leaving the queue over capacity. Check fullness before appending (or remove the appended item before raising).

findings.trigger: a = TaskQueue(2); b = TaskQueue(2); a.put(None); len(b); b.get()
findings.observed: len(b) is 1 and b.get() returns None even though no item was put into b.
findings.expected: Separate instances are independent, so len(b) is 0 and b.get() raises IndexError.
findings.explanation: The mutable default items list is shared by every construction that omits items, so operations on one instance change other instances. Use a fresh list per instance, such as a None default followed by list initialization.
